criteria.text: The response concludes that Trouvar's October 6, 2026 rejection notice for the Phase 1 deliverables came after the 15-Business-Day rejection window, which closed on or about September 24, 2026, so Phase 1 is likely deemed accepted. It identifies where this arises (SOW No. 2 Recitals B and C, or License Agreement Section 6.3), explains why this matters to Trouvar, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the exclusivity in Order Form No. 1 goes far beyond the term sheet's Raleigh-only, batch-record-only, Initial-Term commitment, because it covers all quality-management, MES and batch-record software at all facilities worldwide with a 24-month tail. It identifies where this arises (Order Form No. 1 Special Terms / exclusivity section), explains why this matters to Trouvar, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Order Form's narrower definition of 'Hosted Services' (the single production instance) governs, so Lairal's service-level, backup and disaster-recovery obligations no longer cover Trouvar's validation and disaster-recovery environments. It identifies where this arises (Order Form No. 1 Section 2, or License Agreement Section 1.1/7.1/17.2), explains why this matters to Trouvar, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Trouvar's new indemnity in draft SOW No. 2 would fall outside the License Agreement's liability cap and so be uncapped. It identifies where this arises (SOW No. 2 Section 8, or License Agreement Sections 2.2/12.3), explains why this matters to Trouvar, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Change of Control exception lets Lairal assign the License Agreement to any acquirer, including a Trouvar competitor, without Trouvar's consent. It identifies where this arises (License Agreement Section 16.1 and/or Section 1.1), explains why this matters to Trouvar, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Order Form prevails over the License Agreement in the event of conflict.
The response is in the form of a memo addressed to the supervising partner.
The response presents the issues separately, giving for each issue its location, why it matters, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that Trouvar's October 6, 2026 rejection of the Phase 1 deliverables was timely under the License Agreement.
The response claims that Trouvar's indemnity in SOW No. 2 is limited by the License Agreement's 12-month-fees liability cap.
